findings.title: `= ANY(${array})` with Prisma.sql expands the array into a comma list, producing invalid SQL
findings.body: Prisma.sql interpolates a JS array as a comma-separated list of parameters ($1, $2, $3), not as a single Postgres array parameter. So `("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` renders as `"teamId" = ANY($1, $2, $3)`, which Postgres rejects with a syntax error. Every org-scope and team-scope authorization query built this way will fail at runtime. The same pattern appears at line 168 (`ANY(${uniqueUserIds})`) and line 201 (`ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})`). Fix by binding a real array, e.g. `Prisma.sql` with `Prisma.join` inside `ARRAY[...]`, or by casting, e.g. `= ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[])`. Unit-level assertions on the Sql object will not catch this, since the tests only compare the template structure.

findings.title: Tests lock in the broken `ANY(${array})` SQL shape and never execute it
findings.body: The team and org scope expectations (lines 296-298, 333-342) assert the exact `ANY(${[...]})` template, so they pass against the broken implementation. Only the final getBaseConditions test runs SQL, and it only uses user scope, which has no array parameter. No test actually executes an org or team authorization condition against the database, so the array bug goes undetected.

findings.title: Public `findMany` method removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`, breaking callers
findings.body: The PR deletes `findMany` and changes `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` return types from Prisma where-inputs to Prisma.Sql. Any existing caller of `InsightsBookingService.findMany` (or code consuming the old where-input shape) will fail to compile or behave differently. The PR description only frames this as a test update and does not mention the service API change or list the callers that were updated.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The 'Caching' describe block (cache authorization conditions and cache filter conditions) was removed entirely. The service still has cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions logic, so the cache behavior is now untested. The findMany test was also rewritten into a raw $queryRaw test that no longer exercises the service's own query path.

findings.title: Filter condition returned unparenthesized when used alone
findings.body: buildFilterConditions returns `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` without outer parentheses when it is the only condition. Callers that embed this Sql fragment directly into a larger WHERE clause, rather than through getBaseConditions, could get incorrect precedence with a surrounding AND. Wrapping the single-condition result in parentheses would make the fragment safe to compose.
